$comment: Copy to <Project>/API-Testing/suite.json, then REPLACE every check with checks derived from the REAL Postman collection / spec (SETUP.md §1) — this file documents the FORMAT against an imaginary notes API on an example host. Placeholders in any string: {env.NAME} = environment variable (secrets never appear as literals), {cap.name} = a value captured by an earlier check (chain through returned values, never hardcoded ids), {runId} = this run's id (test data is run-id-prefixed per TEST_DATA_RULES). A `capture` path is an implicit exists-assertion: if the response lacks it, the check FAILS. Checks run in order; a check whose {cap.*} source did not pass is skipped, and any skipped/errored check makes the run blocked — never a pass. Keep ids as the project's real TC-NNN where cases exist: those rows feed results[] in the run-result. Every check names its oracle.

oracle.source: the Postman collection / OpenAPI spec the checks were derived from

checks.name: no token on a write → 401 with an error body (negative first: a suite with only happy paths tests the demo, not the API)

oracle.source: auth section of the spec — every write requires a bearer token

checks.name: create note → 201, body echoes what was sent (200 OK alone is not an oracle)

oracle.source: POST /notes in the collection — 201 + the created resource in the body

checks.name: created note is readable, chained via the returned id
another user's token on my note → 404 (a 200 here is an IDOR — file it with tag SECURITY)

oracle.source: authorization model — resources are per-user; 403 or 404 per the spec, 200 never

checks.name: bad input → documented 422 + a useful error body, not a 500

oracle.source: validation rules in the spec — title is required

checks.name: delete → 204 (doubles as teardown — the suite cleans up what it created)
